01 / Overview

What should a driving world model predict?

AffordDrive3D connects future appearance with spatial structure and action-relevant regions. Explore how these predictions relate to planning in the same driving scene.

Same scene. Different decisions.Seeing the future is not enough. A driving policy also needs to understand where it can safely move.

World predictions

Planning outcomes

HumanDriveVLA-W0AffordDrive3D
From appearance to action-relevant spatial understanding.

AffordDrive3D additionally predicts future geometry to capture evolving spatial structure, alongside drivable areas and collision-critical regions relevant to ego motion. Together, these predictions align future world modeling more closely with trajectory planning.

Qualitative comparison with DriveVLA-W0 (RGB world supervision). The animation stages the available predictions; the trajectory images and per-scene PDMS are from the paper, not a simulated live rollout. The colors distinguish the methods and do not recolor their plotted trajectories.

02 / Method

The AffordDrive3D framework

A causal VLM processes multi-view images, navigation commands, ego state, and four groups of learnable tokens. Explore each branch to see how it contributes to planning.

What matters for motion

Temporal affordance forecasting

Affordance tokens predict drivable-area and collision-critical maps for the current frame and eight future timestamps, linking spatial prediction directly to ego motion.

27 tokens2 dense maps0–4 s horizon

03 / Results

Planning performance on NAVSIM

AffordDrive3D achieves 91.3 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 89.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, exceeding every baseline in the paper’s comparisons.

04 / Qualitative results

Driving affordances in context

Selected predictions from two driving scenarios, highlighting road structure and collision-relevant regions.

Narrow curvy road

Following the drivable road

The drivable-area predictions capture the narrow road structure as it curves ahead, providing spatial cues about where the ego vehicle can move.

Leading vehicle braking

Anticipating collision risk

Collision-critical predictions highlight the leading vehicle across future horizons. RGB-consistent depth captures its relative distance and the surrounding scene geometry.
